scope: Common local Chromium Download methods, events and acceptDownloads policy on native macOS arm64/Bun 1.4.2. No release or performance acceptance.

cleanup.scope: Download differential and viewer subprocess watchdogs. The complete core run had no outer watchdog; individual core checks retain their own supervision.

changes: Context-owned GUID identities retain original Page and metadata. Normal contexts accept by default; explicit denial publishes metadata but rejects file access.
Driver wire-order preparation preserves already-admitted cancellation outcomes across later context retirement without admitting new closed-context operations.
Started filesystem jobs own original locks, credits, browser leases and guardian liveness through OS completion. Queued expired/cancelled work cannot start later.
Chromium creates the context download directory on first use. Guardian custody survives browser exit while physical work remains; driver death releases cleanup.
Streams retain context ownership and detach listeners when underlying streams close. Context closure or successful deletion reports TargetClosedError to active readers.
Metadata-only tracing records all six asynchronous Download methods and download event waits with original page/caller identity, complete boundaries and no DOM captures.
retainedDevelopmentAttempts: Initial characterization used too few initial response bytes to trigger Chromium downloads and failed four active-transfer cases. Corrected fixture bytes and waiter observation are retained.

The pinned reference stream can reject asynchronously inside _read and hang consumption after context closure. A bounded characterization preserves that failure; Flashwright intentionally reports an observable stream error.

The first shared traced run exposed accepted saveAs losing its original owner before first polling. Synchronous wire-order preparation fixed the race; controlled native tests retain unpolled path/save cases.
The first broad core run passed 103 groups before a stale parity source hash stopped group 104. Metadata was refreshed and the complete final snapshot rerun.

Preserved SVGOMG tests pass 6/6 on the reference and 5/6 on Flashwright. Download passes; open-svg evaluation in an out-of-process frame remains explicitly unsupported. This is a retained failure, not full migration acceptance.
limitations: No out-of-process frame, popup fallback, remote browser or persistent-context Download claim.
Metadata and physical job limits are bounded; no hard disk-byte quota or 64-job saturation acceptance is claimed.
Saved copies use ordinary filesystem copying, not atomic replacement.
Pinned reference archives omit Download calls; candidate metadata is additional diagnostic coverage, not identical trace layout.
Context-close-active is functionally tested without trace recording; other archives finalize before context teardown.
Controlled download publication integration coverage remains narrower than all possible page/context allocation races.
Native Linux measurements remain unverified. Fresh matched performance, broader migration/consumer coverage and release gates remain open.
evidenceNormalization: Only workstation path strings and dependent hashes change; numeric/boolean/null observations remain exact. Raw trace archives/screenshots remain private at recorded hashes; regenerated artifacts have new identities.
